problems.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the number of **good subarrays** of `nums`.

A **good array** is an array where the number of **different integers** in that array is **exactly** `k`.
problems.approach_brute: Enumerate all subarrays and count distinct with a set. O(N^2) or O(N^3).
problems.approach_optimal: exactlyK = atMost(K) − atMost(K−1). The atMost helper uses a sliding window with a hashmap of frequencies. Time O(N), space O(K).

problems.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `k`. A subarray is called **nice** if there are exactly `k` odd numbers on it. Return the number of nice subarrays.
problems.approach_brute: Enumerate every subarray, count odds. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: Reduce odds=1, evens=0. Count subarrays with sum exactly K via atMost(K) − atMost(K−1). Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
problems.description: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `goal`, return the number of non-empty subarrays with a sum equal to `goal`.
problems.approach_brute: Two nested loops over all subarrays. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: atMost(goal) − atMost(goal-1) via sliding window, OR prefix-sum hashmap. O(N).

problems.title: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
problems.description: Given strings `s` and `t` of equal length and an integer `maxCost`. Changing the i-th char of s to t[i] costs `|s[i] - t[i]|`. Return the maximum length of a substring of `s` that can be changed to be the same as the corresponding substring of `t` with total cost <= `maxCost`.
problems.approach_brute: Check every substring with O(N) cost sum. O(N^3).
problems.approach_optimal: Compute c[i] = |s[i]-t[i]|. Find longest subarray of c with sum <= maxCost via sliding window. O(N).

problems.title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
problems.description: Given array `nums` and integer `k`. In one operation, increment any element by 1. Return the maximum possible frequency of an element after at most `k` operations.
problems.approach_brute: For each candidate target, count reachable elements. O(N · max_val).
problems.approach_optimal: Sort. Window [l..r] with target nums[r] needs cost = nums[r]·(r-l+1) - sum. Slide r forward, advance l when cost > k. O(N log N).

problems.title: Maximum Erasure Value
problems.description: You are given an array of positive integers `nums`. Erase exactly one subarray containing only **unique** elements. The score is the sum of erased elements. Return the maximum score.
problems.approach_brute: Enumerate all subarrays, check uniqueness with set. O(N^3).
problems.approach_optimal: Sliding window with a hash set + running sum. On duplicate, advance left removing values until duplicate is gone. Track max sum. O(N).

problems.title: Continuous Subarrays
problems.description: Given a 0-indexed integer array `nums`. A subarray is **continuous** if for every pair of indices i1 < i2 in it, `|nums[i1] - nums[i2]| <= 2`. Return the total number of continuous subarrays.
problems.approach_brute: For each l, expand r until max - min > 2. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: Sliding window with invariant max - min <= 2. Track max/min via two monotonic deques. For each r, count = r - l + 1. O(N).

problems.title: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. Return the number of subarrays where the **maximum element** of `nums` appears **at least** `k` times in that subarray.
problems.approach_brute: For each subarray, count occurrences of the max. O(N^3).
problems.approach_optimal: Find max. Sliding window: maintain count of max in [l..r]. When count >= k, all subarrays starting from any index <= l contribute (n - r) extensions; advance l forward to keep count = k - 1, repeat. O(N).

problems.title: Number of Substrings With Only 1s
problems.description: Given a binary string `s`, return the **number of substrings with only 1's** in it. Since the answer may be too large, return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
problems.approach_brute: For each starting position, count consecutive 1s. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: Each maximal run of L consecutive 1s contributes L*(L+1)/2 substrings. Single linear scan tracking current run length. O(N).

problems.title: Count Vowel Substrings of a String
problems.description: A substring is a **vowel substring** if it consists **only of vowels** (`a`,`e`,`i`,`o`,`u`) and contains **all five vowels**. Given string `word`, return the number of vowel substrings.
constraints: word consists of lowercase English letters
problems.approach_brute: Enumerate all substrings; filter to those with only vowels and all 5 distinct. O(N^3).
problems.approach_optimal: For each maximal vowel-only segment, count substrings containing all 5 vowels via at-most-K (K=5) decomposition: atMost(5) − atMost(4). O(N).

problems.title: Find K-Length Substrings With No Repeated Characters
problems.description: Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, return the number of substrings in `s` of length `k` with no repeated characters.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
problems.approach_brute: For each window of size k, check distinctness via set in O(k). O(N · k).
problems.approach_optimal: Sliding window of size k with frequency map. When map size == k after update, count++. On slide, increment incoming and decrement outgoing. O(N).

problems.title: Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
problems.description: The score of an array is defined as the **product** of its **sum** and its **length**. Given a positive integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the number of non-empty subarrays of `nums` whose score is **strictly less than** `k`.
edge_cases: k smaller than smallest single element
k larger than full sum * n
problems.approach_brute: Enumerate all subarrays computing sum*length. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: Sliding window. For each right, advance left while score >= k. The longest valid window ending at right gives `right - left + 1` valid subarrays ending at right. Sum these contributions. O(N).
